findings.motion: Second Reading (House roll call 758, vote 66 to 47)
findings.note: He voted aye on the second reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) requires a voter registration application to affirmatively state US citizenship before it is processed (new G.S. 163-83, with a 30-day cure by a statement under penalty of perjury), and requires drivers license offices to proceed only if the applicant affirmatively states citizenship. It also directs the State Board of Elections to create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database, and sets weekly removal of deceased voters. The bill page shows it was vetoed 08/17/2026 and placed on the calendar for 09/02/2026. He is not listed as a sponsor.

findings.motion: Motion 11, Concur (House roll 800, vote 74 to 35), State Board of Elections Administrative Changes; became Session Law 2026-60
findings.note: He voted aye to concur on HB 834, later Session Law 2026-60. The text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H834v6.pdf) moves the deadline for a voter without photo ID to bring ID to the county board for a provisional ballot, and for curing absentee ballot ID deficiencies, from the third to the fifth business day after the election. It treats certain Class C drivers licenses as valid unexpired photo ID for voting until 12/31/2027. It also keeps the absentee ballot rule that a photocopy of ID or an ID affidavit must come with the return envelope and can be cured.
